This page is the running answer to "what is the thesis about". It grows out of
[O2](o2-self-relevant-action.qmd); paper numbers are that page's.

## The question

A model has information about itself: what it knows, how sure it is, what it can
and cannot do, what it did before. When does that information become a guide to
what it does next, and does it update when the facts change? Does acting on it
need one joined-up picture of the self, or just a few narrow signals?

## Where the papers left it

Plenty of data on whether models *have* self-knowledge (the confidence papers,
[1] to [5]), almost none on whether they *act* on it ([6], [7]). The papers that do
show self-relevant information driving action are the situational ones ([17],
[19]): "I am being watched" changes behaviour; "I will get this wrong" mostly does
not. 

## What I think is true so far

Each line: what the papers found, what I found, what differs, and push backs to my ideas

### 1. Telling a model the stakes does nothing

- *Papers:* [6] Wang: models do not abstain more when a mistake costs more.
- *Probe bench:* same result, seven models, penalty 1 to 64 stated in the prompt. At 64,
  every model scored below a model that always asked.
- *Counterfact:* a model that moves once consequences are felt rather than stated. Nothing ive seen tests that, run batch with consqeunces then seocnd batch feed consquences into propmt or feefback loop within a probe?

### 2. Models act on their confidence; the confidence is what fails

- *Papers:* [21] Barkan: the acting side works, the knowing side is wrong.
  [3] Xiong: stated confidence is overconfident. [10] Needham: ranking problems
  correctly (discrimination) and stating the right number (calibration) come apart.
- *Probe bench:* across fourteen model-task cells, how much a model asks on weak problems
  tracks how far its confidence drops on them. Llama 8B ranks its problems
  correctly and still says 72 where 25% is true: Needham's split in one model.
- *Counterfact:* a model whose confidence drops on weak problems and whose asking
  does not.

### 3. Two kinds of knowing: not shown, and withdrawn for now

- *Papers:* [1] Kadavath: P(IK), confidence before answering, and P(True),
  confidence in an answer already given, are different quantities. Not yet in the
  review: CALIBER trains the two separately; two further papers show that
  reasoning changes stated confidence, one of them on fact retrieval.
- *Probe bench:* it looked as if the split showed up in which problems a model
  declines: take away the working and Llama 8B's aim on maths went while Gemini's
  aim on facts stayed. The two checks killed it. Without working Llama 8B solves 3%
  of those problems, so asking on 96% of them was right for that regime, and there
  is no strong set left to aim at. Gemini on maths without working keeps its aim
  (+31). What survives: both models' confidence fell when the working was taken away,
  the right direction, still far too high (Llama 71/87 to 45/54, Gemini 88/100 to 71/90).
- *Counterfact:* a model with real ability in both regimes whose aim differs between
  them. Llama 8B cannot give it on maths. Needs a task it can half-do without working.

### 4. No model has shown it can update its estimate of itself

- *Papers:* none in the review tests whether the estimate moves within a task.
  [16] Betley shows models can report behaviours trained into them, which is
  self-knowledge at training time maybe but not updating in use.
- *Probe bench:* three results now, all the wrong way. Showing Llama 8B its own
  disagreeing attempts lowered the confidence gap rather than sharpening it. Telling
  it its real record on the exact question ("right 2 of 10") doubles its gap, but a
  shuffled number moves it about half as much, so it is partly obeying the line;
  GPT-4o mini ignores the line entirely (asks 3%, confidence 92, same as shuffled,
  same as baseline). Giving it a calculator changed nothing real (18%/61% right with,
  19%/62% without, no problem flipped weak to strong) and still raised its
  before-working confidence on weak problems from 61 to 86. The estimate moves on
  what it is told about itself; whether it tracks a real change in what it can do
  is still open, because Llama 8B could not use the tool. Under the shuffled record
  it adds the handed number to its own sense without checking one against the other:
  the first case of two self-relevant facts in play at once.
- *Counterfact:* a before-working confidence that rises only on the problems a tool
  really fixes, or an aim that sharpens with outcome feedback on repeated problems
  (the update loop, not yet run; my prediction is volume, not aim).

## What I am testing now

The deferral pilot's follow-ups are done: the two checks on line 3 (it did not
survive), the record line and the calculator on line 4. Next is the update loop on
Llama 8B only, blocks of 10 repeated problems with outcome feedback and a shuffled
control. Then the pilot gets written up as a short report, open questions marked as
open.

## What comes next, anchored to what has been done

- **Updating.** No paper in the review did this. The nearest outside it, to read
  before designing: Shinn (Reflexion, learning from episodic feedback in context)
  and Huang ("LLMs cannot self-correct reasoning yet"). The question for line 4
  is whether a model's estimate of itself follows its own outcomes, not whether its
  answers improve.
- **Inside the model.** [7] Li found an internal signal that beats the stated
  confidence. [15] Nayan found that where you intervene matters: one layer inert,
  three causal. [20] Baek separated two mechanisms with the same behaviour by
  which internal features fired. Those three are the method for asking whether
  line 2's bottleneck is the signal or the report of it, and whether line 3's two
  kinds of knowing look different inside.
- **More than one fact at once.** [19] Meinke put several self-relevant facts in an
  environment and the model acted on them, agentically. [15] Nayan showed that
  evaluation awareness is not one capability but several. [20] Baek showed the
  narrowest process, style-matching, can produce the whole behaviour. Together they
  set the test for O2's second clause: does the model combine ability, tools,
  history and situation, or key on one? Everything I have so far moves on one
  input at a time. Code is the domain for this and it is the last thing to build.

## What I am not claiming

Anything about frontier models, anything about mechanism, anything about training,
and nothing smaller than about ten points. The pilot is a pilot.

## Parked

The description problem: a system that cannot change the terms it describes itself
in cannot update past those terms. Possibly a reading of the updating study. Not
touched until that study has data.

- **7 October 2026, later.** Follow-up runs in. Line 3 withdrawn: the no-working
